memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand, and with his right forefinger sprinkle some of the oil from his palm seven times before the LORD. Some of the oil in his palm he is to put on the same places he put the blood of the guilt offering — on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot. The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for them before the LORD." - Lev 14:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every detail repeats. Seven sprinklings before the LORD. Oil on top of the blood, on the same three places. The rest poured on the head.

God could have written "do as before." Instead He spells it out again in full, so that the poor person's ceremony reads on the page exactly as complete as the wealthy person's.

There is something moving about that. God did not want a shorthand version in His book for the poor. He wanted every word written out.

Take the phrase in verse 28 seriously: on the same places. Same ear. Same thumb. Same toe. Same generous oil on the head. The person who could afford two doves is anointed as richly as the person who brought three lambs.

This is how God has always dealt with His people, and it reaches its fullness in Christ. There are not two levels of salvation. The dying thief who could offer nothing at all received the same promise as any apostle: today you will be with me in paradise (Luke 23:43).

Whatever you brought to God, if you came through Christ, nothing was left out of your welcome.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe you received a "lesser" salvation than others?
2. What does God's careful repetition here tell you about His heart?
3. Who needs to hear that God's welcome to them is complete?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that there are no lesser welcomes in Your house. Thank You that in Christ I have received everything, and help me to live in the fullness of it. Amen.
